Policy prompt engineering (F,P,C,L,D,M) defines the input layer that generates actionable intelligence, enforcing epistemic humility through explicit 'MISSING:' declarations. The stop-loss mechanism (T,S_L,C) introduces temporal control, ensuring bounded rationality. These interact as a feedback loop: prompts generate state transitions, which inform stop-loss decisions, and vice versa. Failure modes arise when prompts lack integrity (false confidence), or when stop-losses are ignored (strategic drift).
